name: Registry publishing and package configuration (P16 EP-387)
skipReason: Build-and-release configuration, not a runtime surface — there is no route to call. Verified by tests/platform/registryPublishing.test.ts (52 assertions over every package.json, the .npmrc, the changeset and the resolver script), and by the CI drift gate `node scripts/release/normalize-publish-config.js --check`.
description: Makes every vertical-facing @projexlight SDK installable from the private registry. Proves all four criteria. AC1: the fourteen listed packages get private:false (a private package is SKIPPED by npm publish without an error, so a vertical would get a bare 404), a publishConfig, real main/types (without which the install succeeds and every import fails — a worse failure than not installing) and a files list that ships dist plus src/db/migrations, since the migration runner reads those .sql files at gateway boot and omitting them would install cleanly then run the service against an unmigrated schema. AC4: publishConfig.registry is deliberately ABSENT everywhere. npm resolves the publish target as publishConfig.registry > .npmrc scope registry > default, so the hardcoded http://localhost:4873/ that all 24 pre-existing publishConfigs carried would have BEATEN anything CI set — a production release would have published to a developer laptop and reported success. The scope registry now lives only in .npmrc, and scripts/release/set-registry.js resolves dev vs prod without mutating that tracked file (a release that rewrites .npmrc leaves the tree dirty and silently points the next developer's install at production). AC2: a changeset accompanies the release, bumping all fourteen minor — minor rather than patch because going from unpublishable to publishable is new consumable surface, and not major because no existing API changed; the test also asserts the changeset config does not ignore any of them, since an ignored package never gets bumped and consumers keep resolving a stale build. AC3: the publishable set is the TRANSITIVE CLOSURE of the listed packages, not the list. That distinction was found by a failing test: sdk-conversation depends on @projexlight/db-runtime, and publishing only the former means `pnpm add @projexlight/sdk-conversation` succeeds and then cannot resolve db-runtime, leaving a consumer no option but to vendor the source — the exact outcome this epic exists to end. The closure walk brought 46 packages in, including db-runtime, redis-runtime, sdk-vault, sdk-meter and sdk-pool-router.

testCases.name: All fourteen listed packages are publishable with resolvable entrypoints
No package hardcodes a registry, so production and dev can differ
The resolver returns different registries for dev and prod
Every workspace dependency of a publishable package is itself publishable
A changeset bumps every listed package and none is ignored

errorCases.name: Drift in publishConfig fails the CI gate
errorCases.when: a package is added or edited so its publishConfig, private flag, entrypoints or files list no longer match the normaliser — `--check` exits non-zero rather than rewriting, so CI fails instead of producing a dirty tree

errorCases.name: An unknown release environment fails loudly rather than defaulting
errorCases.message: unknown environment '<env>' — expected one of: dev, prod
errorCases.when: set-registry.js is called with anything but dev or prod; defaulting silently would let a typo publish to the wrong registry
